textArea.b: Team 709 · Stemma, the family health tree

g.textArea: TECH 5900 Product Studio · Section 7 · Raj Kashikar · Viha Srinivas · Unser Jaffry
Oral review with our coach Oct 12–23, 2026 · one PDF due Oct 23, 2026 · analysis as drafted Oct 6, 2026 (revised after review)

The product in one line. A patient builds a three-generation family health tree before a first cardiology visit. Relatives fill in their own branches from a text link (and can share one fact from their own patient portal). Every answer keeps its source and status (known, conflicting, unknown, declined). The patient reviews a one-page summary, and the practice gets a care-team copy the clinician can act on. Free for patients; cardiology practices pay.
Live prototype, synthetic data only: https://stemmahealth.vercel.app

How to read this. [n] is a numbered source in docs/research.md. [S#] is a source opened for the pitch work (Oct 6, 2026). Both lists, with URLs, are in the three Sources frames (see the board map). Interview IDs (ID002, ID006, ID007, ID010, D021) match the Team Hub "Interview Logs". "(note)" means the note-taker's wording; words in quotation marks are only those the Team Hub notes put in quotation marks. Assumption marks our own estimate, with its math. Tags follow the course: N = new, O = old, N/O = some of each.

Board map: Step 1 canvas · Why each Post-it · Step 2 · Step 3 · Mockup screens · Step 4 · Step 4 verdict · Step 5 · Step 5 verdict · Business logic · Configuration · Wedge · Riskiest claim · Choices and open items · Sources

textArea.b: Step 4 verdict: Will people buy it?

g.textArea: Use: yes, if the practice sends the link. Buy: not yet shown. Patients gain the most against what they use today, and clinic-sent pre-visit tools get finished (57% of 95,166 invited finished one [92]). No practice manager, cardiologist or relative is among our 21 logged interviews, so payment and clinician value are unproven.

textArea.b: Step 5 verdict: Can we make it?

g.textArea: Yes at pilot scale, from about January 2027; not yet a business that pays salaries. The patient-to-clinician flow runs today on synthetic data; the pilot backend is next. Running it under BAAs costs about $689–834 a month. At $500 per cardiologist per year, 17–21 paying cardiologists cover that; one salary (wage only) needs about 290, roughly every independent cardiologist in NYC. Founder support time (1–2 hours per practice a month) is unpaid and not in that cost.

cardiology practices need which relative, what condition and what age, their intake forms take it from memory, and a link they send gets those details, each with its source, into the chart before visit one.

the patient side already runs on public standards, a PDF reaches any chart, and a pilot on vendors that sign BAAs costs under $850 a month, which about ten two-cardiologist practices cover with founders unpaid.

Independent NYC cardiology groups (2–10 cardiologists) pay; their adult new patients use it free; relatives answer by link; the care-team page reaches the practice by read-only link or fax, as a PDF; a $1,000 12-week founding pilot credited to year one, then $500 per cardiologist per year.

3 independent NYC cardiology groups (2–10 cardiologists); all adult new patients (one link in the new-patient paperwork), sharpest for palpitations, fainting, chest pain or high cholesterol. Success: at least 40% of invited new patients whose first visit falls in pilot weeks 2–12 have a patient-reviewed summary in the chart before that visit (read at weeks 6 and 12).

A practice manager will pay. Test by Oct 23: 5 practice-manager conversations with a one-page price card. Pass = 3 of 5 name the budget owner and accept $500/yr in principle, and 1 signs a non-binding letter of intent naming a target start month. The paid letter follows once we have a company, a BAA template and insurance.
